title: Test that a change to a security-sensitive path cannot merge without code-owner approval
description: In OnFinance/mongodb-mcp-server, open a throwaway pull request that changes a comment in a file under .github/workflows/. Have it approved by a reviewer who is not in the owning team. Confirm GitHub blocks the merge, then get approval from a member of the owning team and confirm the merge becomes allowed. Close the PR without merging. Repeat in OnFinance/onfinance_db_model_master with a comment-only change under onfinance_db_model_master/. Attach screenshots or the `gh pr view --json reviewDecision,mergeStateStatus` output as evidence. No production system is touched, and no deployment window is needed.
acceptanceCriteria: For each repository, `gh pr view <n> --json reviewDecision,mergeStateStatus` shows reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED and mergeStateStatus BLOCKED after approval by a non-owner.
For each repository, the same command shows reviewDecision APPROVED after approval by a code-owner team member, and the test PR is then closed unmerged.
The command outputs for both repositories are attached as task evidence.

verificationMethod.description: The CISO repeats the steps in the description on both repositories. Expected: merge is blocked (mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED) when only a non-owner has approved, and unblocked (reviewDecision APPROVED) once a member of the owning ExampleCo team approves. Both test PRs end closed unmerged.

rootCause.description: Nobody ever tested that the chain of command for code approvals works, so the catch-all upstream ownership and the unenforced policy went unnoticed until the probe-sdlc review.
